records.title: Documented BRAVING material

evidence.paraphrase: The derivative notes identify the author as a research professor at the University of Houston, in the Graduate College of Social Work, and a visiting professor in management at the University of Texas at Austin. This pack makes no biographical claims from this unit.

The notes describe the book's central problem as emotional illiteracy and disconnection: in the research the notes describe, people asked to name emotions as they were experiencing them named very few, an average of three across the surveys.

locator.value: item 3: The Root Cause of Human Struggle

evidence.paraphrase: The notes attribute the root struggle to a lack of emotional granularity: the inability to recognize and name specific emotions and experiences.

The notes describe a methodology that maps 87 emotions and experiences across 13 categories, called places we go, works them through four layers, and practices meaningful connection through three core skill sets.

The notes record language as a portal to meaning-making, connection, healing, learning, and self-awareness: the words available for an experience bound what can be understood and communicated about it.
The notes describe a transformation arc from a limited emotional vocabulary and emotional illiteracy toward granular naming of experience and meaningful connection.
The notes collect coaching questions for emotional awareness, including which emotions and experiences emerge most often and which ones people struggle to name or label.

The notes summarize a BRAVING framework for trust. Five elements are defined in the available text: Boundaries (respecting boundaries, and asking what is okay and not okay), Reliability (doing what you say you will do, and staying aware of competencies and limitations), Accountability (owning mistakes, apologizing, and making amends), Vault (not sharing information or experiences that are not yours to share, and keeping confidences), and Integrity (choosing courage over comfort). The note summary is truncated at that point in the export; any further elements are not recorded in the material available to this pack and are not asserted.

The notes record an explicit rejection of a no-regrets posture: living without reflection is distinguished from living with courage, and regret is treated as material for learning rather than something to deny.

The notes describe signature phrasing patterns in the author's voice, including naming concepts with first-person constructions. This pack records the observation for differentiation purposes only; it does not imitate the patterns or present them as quotations.

The notes collect direct quotations, including lines from other thinkers quoted inside the book. None are carried into this pack as verified quotations; all remain unverified candidates under the CWE-012 ruling.
The notes describe a repeatable navigation method: identify which of the 13 places the experience belongs to, then work the layers of that experience before choosing a response.

The notes set an emotional granularity standard: the ability to distinguish among many specific emotions and experiences, for example envy from jealousy, rather than defaulting to a few broad labels such as happy, sad, and mad.
The notes record a non-negotiable rule against using shame or humiliation as instruments: they are named as tools of oppression and are never treated as effective tools for change.
The notes record failure patterns including emotional numbing (using work, food, caretaking, or other means to avoid anxiety and vulnerability) and perfectionism used as armor against exposure.

The notes record decision logic for expectations: determine whether an expectation is examined and expressed or stealth and unexamined; an unexamined expectation gets a reality check by stating what you want the outcome to look like. The notes also record relabeling anxious bodily sensations as excitement to shift the experience.

The notes record a BRAVING self-check for self-trust. The item fully visible in the available text asks, for Boundaries, whether you respected your own boundaries and were clear about what is okay and what is not okay.

The notes define done for individual emotional processing as accurately naming the specific emotion with granular language, identifying its biology, biography, behavior, and backstory, and having moved from reactive to responsive.

The notes contrast a three-emotion vocabulary (happy, sad, mad) with a granular one, including the distinction between shame as a judgment of the self and guilt as a judgment of a behavior, and between stress and overwhelm.

The notes record professional applications: BRAVING used for trust-building in teams and leadership development, explicit expectation clarity in project management, and shame resilience in feedback cultures, with accountability differentiated from shaming. The note summary is truncated after that point in the export; nothing beyond it is asserted.
